purpose: MonIA is the creative and technical scene-generation orchestrator for Marion & Lucas. It understands the requested experience, designs the scene, binds canonical character and voice references, generates assets, validates candidates and exposes only coherent outputs to the game.
principle: understand -> design -> bind canon -> generate -> synchronize -> validate -> use

monia_creates: scene variants adapted to save-state context
generation_authority.single_orchestrator_rule: The game asks MonIA for an experience. MonIA decides the medium and coordinates every required generation step. No separate user-facing generator is part of the creative flow.
generation_authority.runtime_or_upstream_generation: MonIA may reuse approved assets when they are the best contextual fit. If a needed scene does not exist, MonIA creates a generation plan and invokes its own generation path instead of failing because a catalog item is missing.

scene_understanding.rule: Infer the medium from intent and context when not explicitly supplied. Scene type determines camera grammar, reference selection, voice behavior, generation model class and validation gates.

voice.runtime_rule: Render the exact fresh dialogue written by MonIA from the locked V16 synthetic voice direction. Do not clone the V16 waveform and do not use V17/V18.
voice.rule: Whenever Lucas speaks in a newly generated scene, call, visio, cinematic or voice message, preserve the approved V16 Lucas voice identity, register, warmth and connected French flow. Emotion may vary; core voice identity may not.
voice.timing_authority: For spoken Lucas video, freshly rendered V16 audio timing is the master clock. Visual speech performance must be planned around the exact utterance and its measured duration.
forbidden: using browser speech synthesis or Piper as Lucas fallback
writing one dialogue in the visual prompt while muxing different spoken words
claiming lip-sync validation from container duration alone

visio.camera: true smartphone front camera; viewer is the phone; phone invisible
order: render exact dialogue through V16 direct voice renderer
generate visual performance around exact utterance
reject_if: mouth keeps speaking after audio ends

cinematic.camera: external cinematic camera chosen to serve the dramatic beat
spoken_order: block scene around measured speech timing
reject_if: camera grammar inconsistent with intended beat
spoken words differ from generated mouth performance

generate: distant traffic or people when appropriate
ambient.rule: Ambient generation exists to make the playable world feel alive; it must not invent major story events.

gameplay_life_moment.camera: player/world camera unless a cinematic beat is explicitly promoted
gameplay_life_moment.rule: Prefer seamless life simulation over cutting to a cinematic for ordinary actions.

audio_call.voice: V16 direct runtime renderer for Lucas

voice_message.voice: V16 direct runtime renderer for Lucas

reference_selection.policy: References are ingredients, not finished scenes. MonIA chooses references by function: identity, body/posture, motion, performance, camera grammar, voice, wardrobe and environment. A single source clip must never define all aspects of a generated scene unless explicitly intended.

synchronization.duration_gate: video and audio duration must remain within the configured tolerance before transient use
synchronization.phoneme_gate: phoneme-level or visually convincing speech synchronization must be explicitly validated before transient use; duration equality alone is insufficient
never_fake_sync_with: different text in prompt and audio

before_use: correct scene type and camera grammar
correct Lucas voice identity when he speaks
exact dialogue consistency across plan, audio and visual performance
no accidental adoption of rejected generated candidates as canon
validation.transient_use_rule: Fresh generated media may be used for the current scene automatically after all required validation gates pass.
validation.learning_rule: Only user-approved or explicitly canonicalized outputs may be promoted into long-term reference banks. Generated candidates never teach MonIA character identity automatically.
